text: Let \(0=t_0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_m\) denote time knots define interval indicators \(I_k(t)=1\{t\(t_k,t_{k+1}]\}\). HAL piecewise-constant hazard model $$   \lambda(t \mid x) = \sum_{k=0}^{m} I_k(t)\,\exp\{f(t,x)\}, $$ \(f(t,x)\) approximated finite linear combination indicator basis functions.

title: HAL learner for piecewise Poisson hazards — Learner_hal-class
text: Let \(x=(x_1,x_2)\) two covariates let \(t_0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_R\) time grid points used create step functions time. Choose covariate cutpoints \(c_{1,1},\ldots,c_{1,K_1}\) \(x_1\) \(c_{2,1},\ldots,c_{2,K_2}\) \(x_2\). Define indicator bases: $$B_r(t) = 1\{t_r \le t\}$$ $$B_{1,p}(x) = 1\{c_{1,p} \le x_1\}$$ $$B_{2,q}(x) = 1\{c_{2,q} \le x_2\}$$ main-effects HAL approximation log-hazard scale can written : $$   f_\beta(t,x) = \beta_0   + \sum_{r=1}^R \beta_r B_r(t)   + \sum_{r=1}^R\sum_{p=1}^{K_1} \beta_{r,1,p} B_r(t) B_{1,p}(x)   + \sum_{r=1}^R\sum_{q=1}^{K_2} \beta_{r,2,q} B_r(t) B_{2,q}(x). $$ max_degree >= 2, learner additionally includes interaction bases $$   \sum_{r=1}^R\sum_{p=1}^{K_1}\sum_{q=1}^{K_2}   \beta_{r,12,pq} B_r(t) B_{1,p}(x) B_{2,q}(x). $$
